title: Kollio document
description: A versioned, portable, renderer-independent document. No SwiftUI, AppKit or platform type ever appears here.

schemaVersion.description: 2 added `sources`, 3 added `claims`, 4 added `clarifications`, 5 added `comparisons`, 6 added `summaries`, 7 added `history`, 8 added `experiments`, 9 added the document `title`. A file written before any of them is a document without them, not a broken one.

title.description: The user-authored document title. Files written before schema 9 open with the default title.

revision.description: Bumped on every accepted mutation, presentation included.

semanticRevision.description: Bumped only when the meaning of the document changed.

content.description: Semantic objects, keyed by stable object id.

decisions.description: Durable project memory. Survives quitting, reloading and undo-stack loss.

contributions.description: Reusable contributions. Visual duplication never creates a new one.

sources.description: Source references and the citations made from them. Empty in a document with no sources.

claims.description: Claims with an explicit scope and a stance. Absent before version 3.

clarifications.description: Questions intelligence asked, and the state of their answers. Absent before version 4.

summaries.description: Syntheses prepared for handing over. Absent before version 6. A summary is a derivative: it carries the revision it read and a section may be present with no lines, which is how the format says 'nothing was recorded here' rather than 'nothing was written yet'. Those are different claims and the schema keeps them apart by allowing an empty section to exist at all.
Keyed by synthesis id in the alternating `[id, value]` form the codec uses for a keyed container of single-value keys, exactly like `sources`, `claims`, `clarifications` and `comparisons`.

comparisons.description: Comparisons of directions, criterion by criterion. Absent before version 5. A comparison keeps the references each cell rests on, and a cell with no measure may hold no number: the schema states both, so a file that carried a rating without a measure would not validate.
Keyed by comparison id in the alternating `[id, value]` form the codec uses for a keyed container of single-value keys, exactly like `sources`, `claims` and `clarifications`.

experiments.description: Validation experiments built on the reasoning. Absent before version 8. An experiment is the block a person commits to before running anything: a question, a method, a success criterion, the evidence it will be judged against, and an append-only list of revisions so the criterion as it stood before a result stays readable. An overdue date is not a failure and an unrecorded conclusion stays unknown: the type carries no outcome, not even a default.

Keyed by experiment id in the alternating `[id, value]` form the codec uses for a keyed container of single-value keys, exactly like `sources`, `claims`, `clarifications`, `comparisons` and `summaries`.

history.description: What a person did, in order. Absent before version 7, and a document may legitimately have none: the ledger is an audit trail, not the truth, and it cannot be replayed.

targetObjectID.description: The reasoning this experiment validates. Attached to the reasoning, never to a board.

expectedEvidence.description: Objects the document already holds that the result will be judged against. Every id names a real object; the command layer refuses a link to a thing that is not there.

dueDate.description: Optional, and never a status. An overdue date is not a failure.

isSimulation.description: A simulation is labelled as one.

results.description: Results recorded against the block, oldest first, append-only. There is no edit: the observation a person wrote is a record, and a record that can be rewritten is a draft. The newest is the one a reader reads; the ones before it stay readable.

findings.description: Learnings proposed from those results. A learning lands as proposed; accepted means it names a real decision in the document, and nothing here manufactures one.

observation.description: What the person saw after running something. Kept apart from the outcome: they are both required, they are not each other, and nothing derives one from the other.

limits.description: What the run could not do. The second half of missing data being visible.

unit.description: A measurement without a unit is not a measurement, it is a coincidence with a decimal point.

_0.description: The stance on the criterion. Neither value is a truth claim about the world; only a further decision says what follows.
Data insufficient, named. There is no validity percentage anywhere in this format, because an invented one is worse than no answer.

revisionIndex.description: The result it learned from, by position in the append-only list.

acceptedByDecision.description: Accepting a learning means naming a decision that already exists. A decision made here would be a decision in disguise.

localizedText.description: Authored text. `text` is the source; `variants` holds only explicitly authored variants, never machine translations.

anchor.description: Attachment point in object-local unit space, so a connector follows its object.

sourceReference.description: A pointer to a resource, never a copy of it. `locator` is where the bytes actually are.

sourceRevision.description: One state of a source, as it was read. History is kept so a claim stays checkable against what it was based on.

digest.description: How a person is told the text is not what their claim was based on.

extraction.description: What the app could actually get. `noText` is a real, useful answer: an image-only PDF has none.

citation.description: A claim attached to a place in an exact revision. `revisionID` is immutable on purpose.

lineRange.description: A Swift Range<Int>, encoded by Foundation as lowerBound/upperBound.

verificationStatus.description: There is no `verified` case without an observation and an author. A badge a program can set by itself means nothing.

claim.description: What is asserted, where it applies, and how it stands. A constraint only ever blocks inside its own scope.

criterion.description: Optional: what would count as settling it.

claimScope.description: Where a claim applies. Never empty: an unscoped claim would apply to everything.

objectIDs.description: The objects the claim is about.

evidence.description: An observation and an author. There is no case for a bare verdict.

hypothesisAssessment.description: How a hypothesis stands. There is no case meaning `true`: `supported` says something backs the claim, which is not the same as the claim being correct.

constraintResolution.description: Whether a constraint is met. `notApplicable` is a real answer and is not satisfaction.

clarification.description: A question and its answer. `unknown` is a real answer and is not an empty one.

isObsolete.description: The document moved on. The answer is kept, not discarded.

measure.description: What a number would have to be measured against. Required before a criterion may hold a number.

unit.description: The unit the person wrote. No conversion is implied.

higherIsBetter.description: Which way a bigger number is better. Stated, never guessed.

measure.description: Null means judged in words, which is a real state.

weight.description: Null means unweighted. There is no default weight, and a total is undefined without one.

references.description: What the cell rests on. Part of the cell, so a comparison cannot be read without being checkable.

referenceRevisions.description: The source revision each source reference was read against, by source id.

referenceFingerprints.description: The semantic fingerprint of each referenced object when the cell was recorded. A cell whose object has since been edited is a cell about a different sentence.

directionIDs.description: Two or more. A comparison of one direction is refused, not offered.

keptDirectionIDs.description: Explicit and cumulative. Keeping one direction never removes another.

isDraft.description: True until the criteria are confirmed. A draft accepts no cell at all.

comparisonValue.description: A discriminated value rather than the synthesised associated-value form, so a person reading the file can see what kind of value it is. `notRecorded` is a first-class state, so a missing value is never a zero; a number is only reachable when the criterion carries a measure, which the command layer enforces.

title.description: Never empty. A synthesis with no title cannot be found in a list of deliverables.

uncertainties.description: May be a single section with no lines and `isNothingRecorded` true. AC02: 'nothing is known to be uncertain' is a finding and the format has to be able to say it.

baseSemanticRevision.description: AC03: the document revision this synthesis read. Without it a synthesis cannot answer whether it is still true.

isDraft.description: True until confirmed. A confirmed synthesis has said something about every section or declared that there was nothing to say.

originalText.description: AC01: the text as first produced, kept when a person edits the line. Present only after an edit, which is what makes 'the initial text stays intact' checkable rather than asserted.

isNothingRecorded.description: True when the section is empty on purpose. An empty section and a deliberate absence are different claims, and only the second one is allowed to be confirmed.

revisionID.description: The revision that was read, not merely that the source exists. AC03.

decisionIDs.description: The decisions read when the synthesis was written. A later decision on one of these objects is what makes it outdated.

reason.description: Why the wide selection was refused, in words a person can act on.

reversed.description: The id of the entry this one takes back. The target is never removed, which is the point: 'that was undone' and 'that never happened' are different statements and only the second erases the work.

label.description: The menu label the person acted under. The only description of why that exists.

commands.description: Kept verbatim. Empty for a reversal, which names its target instead of carrying the commands again.
